response.sql:
WITH equipment_avgs AS (
  SELECT 
    equipref,
    AVG(humepct) as avg_humidity
  FROM scanenvironment
  WHERE humepct IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY equipref
),
overall_avg_cte AS (
  SELECT AVG(humepct) as overall_avg
  FROM scanenvironment
  WHERE humepct IS NOT NULL
),
above_avg_equipment AS (
  SELECT ea.equipref, ea.avg_humidity
  FROM equipment_avgs ea
  CROSS JOIN overall_avg_cte oa
  WHERE ea.avg_humidity > oa.overall_avg
),
above_avg_group_mean_cte AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_humidity) as group_mean
  FROM above_avg_equipment
)
SELECT 
  aae.equipref,
  aae.avg_humidity,
  aae.avg_humidity - oa.overall_avg as exceeds_all_avg,
  aae.avg_humidity - agm.group_mean as exceeds_group_mean
FROM above_avg_equipment aae
CROSS JOIN overall_avg_cte oa
CROSS JOIN above_avg_group_mean_cte agm
WHERE oa.overall_avg IS NOT NULL
  AND agm.group_mean IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY 
  exceeds_group_mean IS NULL,
  exceeds_group_mean DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: "The average across all equipment" refers to the mean of all individual humidity readings in scanenvironment, not the mean of per-equipment averages. This is the standard interpretation of "overall average."

"Return nothing if either reference average is missing" means return an empty result set if the overall average or the group mean is NULL. This prevents meaningless results when there are no records or no above-average equipment.

alternatives.interpretation: "The average across all equipment" could mean the arithmetic mean of each equipment's average humidity (rather than the mean of all raw readings). This would group-normalize differently if equipment have unequal numbers of readings.
